GET /verified-domains/{domain_name} response has no 'id' property at all; the record's own identity IS the domain string.

Mailchimp's report-side and list-member-activity sub-objects identify each row by 'email_id' -- the MD5 hash of the lowercased subscriber email (see Configuration.AddressingConventionNote), not a vendor-issued surrogate 'id'.

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: The OpenAPI spec's own securityDefinitions declares exactly one scheme: {basicAuth: {type: basic}}, applied via `security: [{basicAuth: []}]` at the document root -- confirmed identical on every one of the spec's 181 paths. Vendor prose (mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/docs/fundamentals/, 'Authenticate with an API key or OAuth 2 token') states the SAME credential (an API key OR an OAuth2 token -- 'We'll refer to both as tokens') can be sent EITHER as HTTP Basic Auth (username = any string, password = the token) OR as a Bearer header -- both are documented, interchangeable transports for the identical credential value. AuthFlow is set to the spec-declared, primary scheme ('basic'); the Bearer alternative is recorded in BearerAlternate below (NOT a second credential class, just a second header shape for the same token).
Configuration.AuthHeaderPatternNote: Verbatim from the vendor's own curl example (fundamentals.html, 'Basic HTTP Authentication' code block): `curl --request GET --url 'https://<dc>.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/' --user 'anystring:TOKEN'`. The username portion is any non-empty string (commonly 'anystring' or the account email in community examples); only the password (the API key or OAuth2 token) is checked.

BearerAlternate.note: Documented as an equally valid transport for the SAME credential value (fundamentals.html 'Bearer Authentication' code block: `--header "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"`). Not a separate OAuth2 bearer-token grant -- the token bytes are identical to what Basic Auth's password slot carries.

OAuth2Alternate.note: Separate multi-tenant 'act on behalf of another user's account' flow (mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/guides/access-user-data-oauth-2/), distinct from the single-account API-key path that is this build's provisioned credential class. GET authorizeUrl?response_type=code&client_id=<CLIENT_ID>&redirect_uri=<REDIRECT_URI> -> redirect carries ?code=... -> POST tokenUrl exchanges the code for an access_token -> GET metadataUrl (with 'Authorization: OAuth <access_token>') returns the account's data-center prefix (dc) needed to build the API base URL. Requires an OAuth app registered in Mailchimp's developer portal (client_id/client_secret).

Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: Explicitly documented as NOT NEEDED: 'Mailchimp Marketing access tokens do not expire, so you don't need to use a refresh_token. The access token will remain valid unless the user revokes your application's permission to access their account.' (access-user-data-oauth-2 guide). This applies to OAuth2 access tokens; the API-key credential class (this build's provisioned type) is likewise a long-lived, admin-issued, non-expiring secret revoked only by manual regeneration in the Mailchimp UI. Left null (not fabricated) per the InferredFromContext-rejected-for-hard-constraints rule -- there IS a documented statement here, so this is ExplicitStatement evidence for the ABSENCE of a refresh flow, not a guess.
Configuration.APIBaseURLNote: Every Mailchimp account is reached at a per-account data-center-prefixed host (fundamentals.html: '...com/3.0/. The <dc> part of the URL corresponds to the data center for your account... if your API key is 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde-us6, then...us6...'). Confirmed structurally in the spec too: `host: 'server.api.mailchimp.com'` is itself a non-resolving PLACEHOLDER host (literal string 'server', not a real subdomain) -- sources/openapi.swagger.json host/basePath/schemes. The connector reads the tenant's <dc> from the per-connection Configuration key named 'DataCenter' (NOT baked into this vendor-wide metadata file) and substitutes it into the template. Three documented ways to obtain <dc>: (1) it is the substring after the '-' in an API-key credential; (2) it is visible in the account's admin UI URL (https://<dc>.mailchimp.com/account/api/); (3) for an OAuth2 token, GET the OAuth Metadata endpoint (see OAuth2Alternate.metadataUrl) with the token, which returns the data center in its response.
Configuration.NavigationBaseURLNote: Root Integration.NavigationBaseURL is set to the data-center-prefixed Mailchimp ADMIN UI host (distinct from the API host: 'admin.mailchimp.com', not 'api.mailchimp.com'), confirmed by two live outbound links on the same fundamentals.html page: https://us1.admin.mailchimp.com/account/api/ ('get an API key') and https://us1.admin.mailchimp.com/account/billing-plan/. The '{server}' placeholder is the account's data-center prefix (same value as APIBaseURLTemplate's {dc}), resolved per-connection -- never a baked tenant constant.

PaginationDefaults.note: Uniform across essentially every collection GET in the spec (sampled directly on GET /lists/{list_id}/members, sources/openapi.swagger.json): `count` (query, integer, default 10, maximum 1000) + `offset` (query, integer, default 0, 'the number of records from a collection to skip'). This is Mailchimp's single, vendor-wide pagination scheme -- no cursor/keyset alternative exists anywhere in the spec. A connector should default to a page size well below the 1000 ceiling (e.g. 200-500) to keep individual response payloads manageable, since Mailchimp does not cap `count` server-side below 1000.

Configuration.APIVersioningNote: The version is embedded directly in the fixed basePath: `basePath: '/3.0'` (sources/openapi.swagger.json document root) -- every request path is relative to https://<dc>.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/. No header-based or Accept-header versioning scheme exists in the spec.

IncrementalSyncCapability.note: Per-object `since_*`/`before_*` ISO-8601 query-param filters exist ONLY where the vendor documents them, confirmed directly on two representative objects (sources/openapi.swagger.json): List Members (`since_last_changed`/`before_last_changed` -- 'Restrict results to subscribers whose information changed after/before the set timeframe', plus `since_timestamp_opt`/`before_timestamp_opt` for opt-in date and `since_last_campaign` for last-campaign-relative filtering) and Campaigns (`since_create_time`/`before_create_time`, `since_send_time`/`before_send_time`). This is NOT a uniform vendor-wide watermark field name (unlike e.g. a single `updated_since` convention) -- each IO's own IncrementalWatermarkField must be set individually by ioiof-extractor per-object. Objects with no documented `since_*` param have no vendor-native watermark and must fall back to content-hash idempotency (per connector-code-conventions.md).

Configuration.WebhooksNote: Two distinct webhook object families are documented and COVERABLE: `lists/{list_id}/webhooks` (per-list subscriber-lifecycle events: subscribe/unsubscribe/profile-updated/cleaned/email-changed/campaign-sent, plus BETA SMS events) and `batch-webhooks` (account-level, fired on batch-operation completion). Confirmed via POST /lists/{list_id}/webhooks request body schema and GET/POST /batch-webhooks paths (sources/openapi.swagger.json).
Configuration.WebhooksSignatureAlgorithmNote: UNDOCUMENTED in the credential-free spec. The POST /lists/{list_id}/webhooks request body schema declares only `url`, `events`, and `sources` (no `secret`/`signature`/`hmac`-named property anywhere in the schema -- confirmed by direct key inspection). No signature-verification scheme is stated. Left null rather than guessed; connector-side inbound-webhook handling should not assume an HMAC header is present.
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: POST /batches submits an array of arbitrary sub-operations (method/path/params/body per sub-op, up to Mailchimp's own internal cap -- see BatchOperations.maxOperationsPerBatch); GET /batches/{batch_id} polls status (`pending` -> `preprocessing` -> `started` -> `finalizing` -> `finished`) and, once finished, returns a `response_body_url` to a gzip archive of every sub-operation's individual response. This is the vendor's async bulk-write mechanism, distinct from the `batches` IO itself (the poll-status record, itself a syncable/observable object).

BatchOperations.resultDelivery: response_body_url -- a URL to a downloadable archive of per-operation results, available once status=finished
BatchOperations.maxOperationsPerBatch: UNDOCUMENTED -- the request body schema (`operations` array) declares no `maxItems`/length constraint anywhere in the spec (confirmed by direct schema inspection); no numeric cap is stated on mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/guides/run-batch-operations/ either (page resolved as a client-rendered shell during this audit -- WebFetch/curl could not extract body text, consistent with the marketing-api-conventions page issue already logged in SOURCE_STUDY.md 1.4). Root Integration.BatchMaxRequestCount and Integration.BatchRequestWaitTime are left null per the provable-only rule rather than fabricated.
BatchOperations.pollWaitTimeGuidance: UNDOCUMENTED -- no explicit recommended polling interval/backoff is stated in the credential-free sources audited.

RateLimitPolicy.model: concurrency-cap, not a request-count-per-window token bucket
RateLimitPolicy.onExceed: 429 (documented); "at exceptionally high volumes you may receive an HTTP 429 or 403 without a JSON body"
RateLimitPolicy.note: Verbatim (fundamentals.html, 'Throttling'): 'The Marketing API has a limit of 10 simultaneous connections. You'll receive a 429 error if you reach the limit. At exceptionally high volumes, you may receive an HTTP 429 or 403 without a JSON body.' No `X-RateLimit-*`/`Retry-After` response headers are declared anywhere in the OpenAPI spec (every operation's only documented response beyond 200 is the shared 'default' Problem Detail Document, which carries no rate-limit metadata) and none were found in the fundamentals page's Throttling section. A connector-side RateLimitPolicy must therefore be a STATIC concurrency cap (bound in-flight requests to <=10) rather than a token-bucket derived from response headers -- there is nothing to parse. The vendor's own recommendation is response-caching, not backoff: 'We recommend that you cache frequently accessed values that do not change often in your application's data store.'

ErrorResponseShape.shape: { type: string (URI), title: string, status: integer, detail: string, instance: string }
ErrorResponseShape.note: Every operation's `default` response in the spec references this single shared schema (confirmed on GET /lists/{list_id}/members, identical across all 181 paths). `status` mirrors the HTTP status code; `detail` is the human-readable message; `instance` is a per-occurrence UUID to quote when contacting support. This is the uniform vendor-wide error envelope for every non-2xx response.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: No ETag, If-Match, If-Unmodified-Since, or If-None-Match term appears anywhere in the OpenAPI spec (confirmed by an exhaustive text search over the full serialized spec: 0 occurrences of all four). No optimistic-concurrency mechanism is offered. Conflict handling for a bidirectional sync (if ever enabled) must use snapshot/3-way comparison, not header-based version checks.
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNote: Surveyed DELETE operations across 10 representative object families (campaigns, lists, ecommerce orders, ecommerce products, templates, file-manager files, landing-pages, batch-webhooks, list-webhooks, list-members -- sources/openapi.swagger.json). NINE are HARD delete -- vendor prose explicitly warns of permanent loss (e.g. Delete List: "If you delete a list, you'll lose the list history...unless you exported and backed up your list"). The SOLE named exception is List Members: `DELETE /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash}` summary is literally 'Archive list member', description 'Archive a list member. To permanently delete, use the delete-permanent action.' -- confirmed by a dedicated `POST /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash}/actions/delete-permanent` RPC endpoint existing alongside it. The archive-flag field is `status` (the member's own `status` enum literally includes an `archived` value alongside subscribed/unsubscribed/cleaned/pending/transactional -- confirmed on the GET /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash} response schema). Per-EntityMap DeleteBehavior default should therefore be object-specific: hard-delete-passthrough for 9 of 10 surveyed families, soft-archive (`status='archived'`) for List Members, with the separate permanent-delete action available as an explicit opt-in only.

WriteCapability.create: Yes -- POST on the collection path for the large majority of writable resources (75 POST operations across the spec).
WriteCapability.update: Yes -- PATCH (partial update, 32 operations) for most updatable resources.
WriteCapability.upsert: Yes -- PUT on 7 endpoints functions as add-or-update, most notably `PUT /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash}` (summary literally 'Add or update list member', description 'Add or update a list member.'). PUT is Mailchimp's upsert verb, not a full-replace-only verb.
WriteCapability.delete: Yes -- DELETE (35 operations); see DeleteSemantics for the hard-vs-archive split.
WriteCapability.note: Method distribution across the 181-path spec: GET=149, POST=75, PATCH=32, DELETE=35, PUT=7 (sources/openapi.swagger.json, counted directly). Bidirectional write is technically supported by the API surface but see the discipline note in METADATA_REPORT / the workflow README -- DefaultSyncDirection stays Pull until a client sandbox validates writes.

CustomObjectMarkerPattern.pattern: n/a -- Mailchimp has no user-definable custom OBJECT type
CustomObjectMarkerPattern.note: Every object family in the taxonomy (lists, campaigns, ecommerce entities, templates, landing pages, etc.) is a fixed, vendor-defined schema -- there is no equivalent of a Salesforce/HubSpot-style customer-created custom object. The closest analogue is ecommerce Products/Orders (customer DATA, not customer-defined SCHEMA) and List Merge Fields (customer-defined FIELDS on the fixed List Member object -- see CustomFieldMarkerPattern).

CustomFieldMarkerPattern.marker: n/a -- every row returned by GET /lists/{list_id}/merge-fields IS a per-list custom field by construction; no built-in-vs-custom boolean flag exists
CustomFieldMarkerPattern.addressedBy: tag (a short uppercase code, e.g. FNAME/LNAME/ADDRESS/PHONE for Mailchimp-auto-created defaults, or any admin-chosen tag for genuinely custom fields)
CustomFieldMarkerPattern.surfacedOnRecordsAt: member.merge_fields.{TAG} -- confirmed on the GET /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash} response schema, which includes a `merge_fields` map property
CustomFieldMarkerPattern.note: Checked the full merge-field response schema (sources/openapi.swagger.json, GET /lists/{list_id}/merge-fields/{merge_id}) for a built-in/system/default marker property -- none exists (merge_id, tag, name, type, required, default_value, public, display_order, options, help_text, list_id, total_items, merge_field_limit, _links -- no boolean distinguishing vendor-default tags like FNAME/LNAME from a genuinely admin-created custom tag). Mirrors the same 'every record IS custom by construction, no split flag' shape documented for Zendesk's custom_objects endpoint in that connector's build.

Vendor's own x-doc-structure title is literally 'Classic Automations'; description states it does not include the successor product (Customer Journeys).
Peripheral, third-party-account-dependent surface (per upstream scope decision) -- real, documented endpoints exist but require a live connected site integration most tenants do not provision.
Third-party-account-gated legacy multichannel-campaigns surface (per upstream scope decision).
Utility free-text query endpoints returning already-covered Campaign/Member objects -- alternate access paths, not distinct record types.
Health-check/diagnostic endpoint, not a syncable object collection.
Only a write-only POST action-trigger endpoint exists in this spec version -- zero readable object surface.

Configuration.OutOfScopeObjectFamiliesNote: Recorded here per the run manifest's scopeDecision so a future build can expand scope without re-discovering the reasoning (full evidence per family in SOURCE_STUDY.md §5). No operator scoping was given for this build -- the modeled scope is the full 76-leaf COVERABLE universe; every exclusion above is the ONLY sanctioned narrowing, each independently evidenced.
Configuration.AddressingConventionNote: The `{subscriber_hash}` path parameter used across ~9 nested list-member and report sub-families (activity, activity-feed, events, goals, notes, tags, click-details/members, email-activity, open-details, sent-to, unsubscribed) is the MD5 hash of the lowercased subscriber email address -- NOT a vendor-issued surrogate key passed straight through from a prior GET. A connector building nested URLs for these families must COMPUTE this hash from the member's email (or accept a raw email/contact_id directly, per the spec's own parameter description) rather than treat it as a discovered PK value.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNote: Recommended IF bidirectional sync is ever enabled for a Mailchimp object (NOT the shipped default -- DefaultSyncDirection stays 'Pull'/read-only for every object per the read-first discipline). Justified by ConcurrencyControl='none': Mailchimp has no ETag/If-Match/version field anywhere in the API (confirmed by an exhaustive spec-text search), so a 'MostRecent' conflict-resolution policy has no reliable signal to compare against and is unsafe to recommend. 'DestWins' (MJ's own record wins on conflict) is the safe default in the absence of optimistic-concurrency support; 'SourceWins' or 'Manual' remain valid alternates a specific EntityMap could choose, but neither is better-justified than DestWins by anything in the vendor's own model. Preconditions before bidirectional could be turned on for ANY Mailchimp object: (1) validate writes against a client sandbox/test account first (never against real member data cold); (2) understand the per-object delete semantics before enabling delete-sync (List Members archive via `status='archived'` and are recoverable -- see DeleteSemantics -- but the other 9 surveyed object families are HARD deletes with vendor-stated permanent data loss, so orphan-deletion sync must be opt-in per object, defaulting OFF for the hard-delete families); (3) accept that conflict resolution will be snapshot/3-way comparison only, never header-based optimistic concurrency, given ConcurrencyControl='none'.
